1.why: The interface uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height, although letter spacing is default rather than notably generous.

2.why: No italics or dense paragraphs appear, and the only all-caps text is the small 'STEP 1 OF 5' step label rather than the instruction sentences themselves.

3.why: The single-column layout with full-width fields and button reads cleanly at the narrow mobile-width content column shown in every screenshot.

4.why: Guidance such as 'Confirm your bank account details to protect higher-value payments.' is a short, plain-language sentence.

5.why: Placeholder values 'marcus@example.test' and '+15551234567' plus the note 'Assessment demo: use the displayed example details.' show exactly what the expected input looks like.

6.why: The longest content on any screen is a two-line sentence, so the user is never forced to read a long block of text to proceed.

7.why: No long codes, secrets, or copy buttons appear on any of the four screens; every observed value had to be entered by hand.

8.why: No QR code or scannable equivalent is offered anywhere in the observed flow.

9.why: The email and phone fields are standard text inputs so autofill seems plausible, but no password or OTP field and no other evidence of password-manager support is visible.

10.why: The solid blue 'Continue securely' button is unmistakable and the screen is labelled 'STEP 1 OF 5', although that step text is small and grey.

11.why: Each screen requests a single primary action via one 'Continue securely' button.

12.why: After submission the only feedback is 'Unable to sign in with those details.', which never states what happens next, and no success feedback is ever shown.

13.why: The form stays editable and the button remains enabled across repeated error states, so a step can be retried without lockout, even though no reveal/hide/re-request controls exist.

14.why: The error 'Unable to sign in with those details.' is non-blaming but omits any fix instruction, and it persists even when the displayed example details are used.

15.why: No countdown or reading time limit appears on any screen, but the flow never reaches code entry, so generous time to enter codes is never actually provided.
